title.zh: 卷七十 列傳第四十 應詹 甘卓 卞壼 劉超 鍾雅
title.en: Volume 70 Biographies 40: Ying Zhan; Gan Zhuo; Deng Qian; Bian Kun
title.raw: 卷七十 列傳第四十 應詹 甘卓 卞壼 劉超 鍾雅 Volume 70 Biographies 40: Ying Zhan; Gan Zhuo; Deng Qian; Bian Kun

sentences.zh: 應詹字思遠，汝南南頓人，魏侍中璩之孫也。

translations.literal: Ying Zhan, courtesy name Siyuan, was a native of Nandun in Runan, and a grandson of Ying Qu, Palace Attendant of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhan, whose courtesy name was Siyuan, came from Nandun in Runan; he was the grandson of Ying Qu, who had served Wei as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 詹幼孤，爲祖母所養。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned and was raised by his grandmother.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents while still a boy and was brought up by his grandmother.

sentences.zh: 年十餘歲，祖母又終，居喪毀頓，杖而後起，遂以孝聞。

translations.literal: When he was a little over ten sui, his grandmother also died; in mourning he wasted away so badly that he could rise only with a staff, and he came to be known for his filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: After his grandmother died when he was just past ten, he mourned until his body gave way and he needed a walking stick to stand; word of his filial piety spread.

sentences.zh: 家富於財，年又稚弱，乃請族人共居，委以資產，情若至親，世以此異焉。

translations.literal: His household was rich in wealth, and he was still very young, so he invited his clansmen to live together with him, entrusting them with his property; their feelings were like those of the closest kin, and the world marveled at this on that account.
translations.idiomatic: The family was wealthy, but he was still a child; he asked his kinsmen to share one roof with him and handed his assets into their care, treating them as his nearest kin—an act that struck people of the time as extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 弱冠知名，性質素弘雅，物雖犯而弗之校，以學藝文章稱。

translations.literal: At the capping age he was already well known; by nature he was plain, magnanimous, and refined, and though things might offend him he did not contend with them; he was esteemed for learning, craft, and literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: After his capping he won a reputation; he was steady, broad-minded, and elegant by temperament, slow to take offense when others crossed him, and admired for his scholarship, arts, and writing.

sentences.zh: 司徒何劭見之曰：「君子哉若人！」

translations.literal: Situ He Shao, seeing him, said, “What a gentleman this man is!”
translations.idiomatic: When Situ He Shao met him, he exclaimed, “Here is a true gentleman.”

sentences.zh: 初辟公府，爲太子舍人。

translations.literal: At first he was summoned to office from the princely administration and became Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He first received appointment from the general administration and served as Gentleman Attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫以爲征東長史。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhao, Sima Lun, appointed him Senior Clerk of the East Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao, named him senior clerk on the staff of the eastward expedition.

sentences.zh: 倫誅，坐免。

translations.literal: When Lun was executed, he was implicated and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Lun was put to death, Ying Zhan was stripped of office by association.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎辟爲掾。

translations.literal: The Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, summoned him as a retainer.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, recruited him to his secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時驃騎從事中郎諸葛玫委長沙王乂奔鄴，盛稱乂之非。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuge Mei, Attendant Clerk on the staff of the Cavalry-in-Attendant, had abandoned Prince Sima Yi of Changsha and fled to Ye, loudly denouncing Yi’s faults.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhuge Mei, who served as clerk on the dashing cavalry general’s staff, had left Prince Sima Yi of Changsha for Ye and was loudly blackening Yi’s name.

sentences.zh: 玫浮躁有才辯，臨漳人士無不詣之。

translations.literal: Mei was restless and sharp-tongued; there was not a person of note in Linzhang who did not go to call on him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Mei was volatile yet eloquent, and everyone of standing around Linzhang beat a path to his door.

sentences.zh: 詹與玫有舊，歎曰：「諸葛仁林何與樂毅之相詭乎！

translations.literal: Zhan had old ties with Mei and sighed, saying, “How can Renlin of the Zhuge clan be so unlike the way Yue Yi comported himself!
translations.idiomatic: Zhan had known Zhuge Mei for years and sighed, “How can Zhuge Renlin diverge so wildly from the conduct of Yue Yi!”

sentences.zh: 」卒不見之。

translations.literal: ” In the end he did not go to see him.
translations.idiomatic: He never went to see him.

sentences.zh: 玫聞甚愧。

translations.literal: When Mei heard of this he was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Mei heard, he was mortified.

sentences.zh: 鎮南大將軍劉弘，詹之祖舅也，請爲長史，謂之曰：「君器識弘深，後當代老子於荊南矣。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the South, Liu Hong—Zhan’s maternal grandfather—asked him to serve as senior clerk and said to him, “Your capacity and insight are broad and deep; one day you will take this old man’s place south of the Jing region.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong, General Who Guards the South and Zhan’s grandfather on his mother’s side, invited him as senior clerk and told him, “Your talent and judgment run deep; in time you will succeed me in holding the Jing southlands.”

sentences.zh: 」仍委以軍政。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he entrusted him with military administration.
translations.idiomatic: He then placed military affairs in his hands.

sentences.zh: 弘著績漢南，詹之力也。

translations.literal: Hong achieved merit south of the Han, and it was through Zhan’s efforts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong’s record of achievement in the southern Han basin owed much to Ying Zhan’s exertions.

sentences.zh: 遷南平太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Administrator of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to become administrator of Nanping commandery.

sentences.zh: 王澄爲荊州，假詹督南平、天門、武陵三郡軍事。

translations.literal: When Wang Cheng took charge of Jingzhou, Zhan was provisionally put in command of the armies of Nanping, Tianmen, and Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng, as governor of Jingzhou, temporarily assigned Zhan to supervise military affairs in Nanping, Tianmen, and Wuling.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽傾覆，詹攘袂流涕，勸澄赴援。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell, Zhan rolled up his sleeves and wept, urging Cheng to hurry to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital collapsed, Zhan wept openly, sleeves pushed back, and pressed Wang Cheng to march to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 澄使詹爲檄，詹下筆便成，辭義壯烈，見者慷慨，然竟不能從也。

translations.literal: Cheng had him draft a proclamation; Zhan set brush to paper and finished at once, the wording bold and stirring, so that all who read it were roused—yet in the end Cheng would not follow the advice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng told him to compose a call to arms; the piece flowed from his brush, fierce and stirring, and moved every reader—yet Wang Cheng still refused to move.

sentences.zh: 天門、武陵谿蠻並反，詹討降之。

translations.literal: The ravine tribes of Tianmen and Wuling both rebelled together, and Zhan attacked and brought them to submission.
translations.idiomatic: The “ravine” peoples of Tianmen and Wuling rose together; Zhan campaigned against them and forced their surrender.

sentences.zh: 時政令不一，諸蠻怨望，並謀背叛。

translations.literal: At that time government orders were inconsistent, and the various tribes nursed resentment and together plotted revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Government edicts clashed, the tribes grew resentful, and they conspired to rebel.

sentences.zh: 詹召蠻酋，破銅券與盟，由是懷詹，數郡無虞。

translations.literal: Zhan summoned their chieftains, broke a bronze tally, and swore a covenant with them; thereafter they cherished Zhan, and several commanderies were untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned their headmen, split a bronze tally, and bound them by oath; they came to trust him, and a swath of commanderies stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 其後天下大亂，詹境獨全。

translations.literal: Afterward the realm was in great turmoil, yet the territory under Zhan alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: As the empire slid into chaos, the region he oversaw alone stayed whole.

sentences.zh: 百姓歌之曰：「亂離既普，殆爲灰朽。

translations.literal: The common people sang of him, saying, “Disorder and separation have spread everywhere; we are nearly dust and rot.
translations.idiomatic: The people sang: “Chaos has spread far and wide; we were almost ash and rot.

sentences.zh: 僥倖之運，賴茲應后。

translations.literal: By a stroke of fortune we rely on Lord Ying here.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fortune lets us lean on Lord Ying.

sentences.zh: 歲寒不凋，孤境獨守。

translations.literal: In the year’s cold we do not wither; alone this border holds fast.
translations.idiomatic: Through the bitter season we do not fade; this lone frontier still stands.

sentences.zh: 拯我塗炭，惠隆丘阜。

translations.literal: He lifts us from mud and charcoal; his kindness rises high as hill and mound.
translations.idiomatic: He pulls us from ruin; his kindness looms like hills.

sentences.zh: 潤同江海，恩猶父母。

translations.literal: His moisture is like the rivers and seas; his grace is like that of father and mother.
translations.idiomatic: His bounty floods like the sea; his grace feels parental.”

sentences.zh: 」鎮南將軍山簡復假詹督五郡軍事。

translations.literal: ” General Who Guards the South, Shan Jian, again provisionally assigned Zhan to command the armies of five commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Guards the South Shan Jian likewise put him in temporary charge of five commanderies’ forces.

sentences.zh: 會蜀賊杜疇作亂，來攻詹郡，力戰摧之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Shu bandit Du Chou raised a revolt and came to attack Zhan’s commandery; Zhan fought hard and shattered him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shu rebel Du Chou rose and struck his jurisdiction, Zhan fought fiercely and broke the attack.

sentences.zh: 尋與陶侃破杜弢於長沙，賊中金寶溢目，詹一無所取，唯收圖書，莫不歎之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, together with Tao Kan, he defeated Du Tao at Changsha; gold and jewels filled the rebels’ camp, yet Zhan took nothing for himself and gathered only maps and books, at which everyone sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Tao Kan in crushing Du Tao at Changsha. Treasure glittered everywhere in the captured camp, but Zhan took only charts and books, and onlookers marveled.

sentences.zh: 元帝假詹建武將軍，王敦又上詹監巴東五郡軍事，賜爵潁陽鄉侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan provisionally named him General Who Establishes Might, and Wang Dun further recommended him to oversee military affairs in the five Ba-East commanderies, enfeoffing him as Village Marquis of Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan appointed him acting General Who Establishes Might; Wang Dun also nominated him to supervise the five eastern Ba commanderies and enfeoffed him as village marquis of Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 陳人王沖擁眾荊州，素服詹名，迎爲刺史。

translations.literal: Wang Chong of Chen, who commanded a host in Jingzhou, had long admired Zhan’s name and welcomed him as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chong of Chen, leading a body of men in Jingzhou, had always respected Zhan’s reputation and offered him the governorship.

sentences.zh: 詹以沖等無賴，棄還南平，沖亦不怨。

translations.literal: Zhan regarded Chong and his like as worthless ruffians and withdrew to Nanping; Chong bore him no grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan judged Chong and his followers disreputable adventurers and returned to Nanping; Wang Chong did not resent it.

sentences.zh: 其得人情如此。

translations.literal: Such was the hold he had on people’s hearts.
translations.idiomatic: That was how deeply he commanded people’s regard.

sentences.zh: 遷益州刺史，領巴東監軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Inspector of Yi Province and concurrently Supervisor of the Army in Ba-East.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to inspector of Yi province while continuing as army supervisor in eastern Ba.

sentences.zh: 詹之出郡也，士庶攀車號泣，若戀所生。

translations.literal: When Zhan left the commandery, gentry and commoners clung to his carriage and wailed as if parting from the parents who bore them.
translations.idiomatic: As he left the district, scholars and townsfolk seized his cart and wept as though losing their own parents.

sentences.zh: 俄拜後軍將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed General of the Rear Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after he was named General of the Rear Guard.

sentences.zh: 詹上疏陳便宜，曰：「先王設官，使君有常尊，臣有定卑，上無苟且之志，下無覬覦之心。

translations.literal: Zhan submitted a memorial setting forth what was expedient, saying, “The former kings established offices so that the ruler has a settled dignity and ministers have fixed subordination; above there is no spirit of careless compromise, and below there is no heart of encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: He presented a memorial on practical reform: “The ancient kings set up offices so the sovereign kept constant authority and ministers a clear chain of command—no slack ambition above, no grasping ambition below.

sentences.zh: 下至亡秦，罷侯置守，本替末陵，綱紀廢絕。

translations.literal: Down to the perishing Qin, marquisates were abolished and governors installed; root and branch were reversed, and the whole fabric of rule was cast away.
translations.idiomatic: By the fallen Qin, feudal lords were swept away for commandery magistrates; foundations and branches were inverted and good order collapsed.

sentences.zh: 漢興，雖未能興復舊典，猶雜建侯守，故能享年享世，殆參古跡。

translations.literal: When Han arose, although it could not fully restore the old model, it still mixed enfeoffed nobles with commandery magistrates, and so was able to enjoy long reigns and pass down ages, nearly matching the traces of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: When Han rose it could not wholly revive the classical order, yet it still mixed fiefs with local governors, which is why it enjoyed long reigns almost matching antiquity.

sentences.zh: 今大荒之後，制度改創，宜因斯會，釐正憲則，先舉盛德元功以爲封首，則聖世之化比隆唐虞矣。

translations.literal: Now, after the great desolation, institutions should be remade; we ought to seize this moment to straighten the statutes, first enfeoffing those of supreme virtue and chief merit as the foremost recipients of rank—then the transformation of this sage age could rival Tang and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: After the great ruin we must refashion institutions; this is the time to align the laws, beginning by investing men of towering virtue and signal merit—then our age could stand beside the eras of Tang and Yu.”

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「性相近，習相遠，訓導之風，宜慎所好。

translations.literal: ” He also said, “By nature men are close; by habit they diverge. In the wind of instruction one must be careful what is loved.
translations.idiomatic: He added: “Natures are alike; habits set people apart. In moral education we must watch what we cultivate.

sentences.zh: 魏正始之間，蔚爲文林。

translations.literal: Between the Zhengshi years of Wei it flourished into a forest of letters.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei’s Zhengshi era letters bloomed into a whole grove of talent.

sentences.zh: 元康以來，賤經尚道，以玄虛宏放爲夷達，以儒術清儉爲鄙俗。

translations.literal: From the Yuankang reign onward, the Classics were despised and “the Way” exalted; emptiness and unrestraint were taken for openness, while Confucian learning and sober restraint were scorned as vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuankang on, classics were spurned for abstruse Daoism; idle transcendence passed for sophistication, while Confucian rigor seemed coarse.

sentences.zh: 永嘉之弊，未必不由此也。

translations.literal: The harm of the Yongjia years need not have been unrelated to this.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongjia disaster surely owed something to that fashion.

sentences.zh: 今雖有儒官，教養未備，非所以長育人材，納之軌物也。

translations.literal: Now, although there are Confucian officials, instruction and nurture are not complete; this is no way to rear talent and bring men within the rails.
translations.idiomatic: Today’s Confucian posts lack real schooling; they cannot nurture talent or keep men within bounds.

sentences.zh: 宜修辟雍，崇明教義，先令國子受訓，然後皇儲親臨釋奠，則普天尚德，率土知方矣。

translations.literal: The Biyong academy should be repaired and the teachings of the sages exalted; first let the sons of the state receive training, then let the imperial heir in person attend the libation rite—then all under Heaven will honor virtue, and throughout the realm men will know their proper stations.”
translations.idiomatic: Rebuild the ritual academy, lift the sages’ doctrine, drill the imperial students first, then have the heir apparent preside at the ceremonial libation—so the world esteems virtue and every quarter knows its duty.”

sentences.zh: 」元帝雅重其才，深納之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan greatly valued his talent and accepted his advice in depth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan prized his ability and took his counsel to heart.

sentences.zh: 頃之，出補吳國內史，以公事免。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he went out to fill the vacancy as interior minister of the Wu princedom and was removed for an administrative matter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went out as interior minister of the princedom of Wu and was dismissed over a routine affair.

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍劉隗出鎮，以詹爲軍司。

translations.literal: When General Who Guards the North, Liu Kui, went out to his command, he took Zhan as army director.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Kui, General Who Guards the North, departed for his post, he named Zhan director of his army.

sentences.zh: 加散騎常侍，累遷光祿勳。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and, by stages, rose to Minister of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He also received the title of cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and eventually became minister of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 詹以王敦專制自樹，故優游諷詠，無所標明。

translations.literal: Because Wang Dun monopolized power and built up his own faction, Zhan therefore moved at ease, chanting and versifying, and made no open pronouncements.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Dun wielding unchecked power, Zhan kept his own counsel, drifting through poetry and song without airing a public position.

sentences.zh: 及敦作逆，明帝問詹計將安出。

translations.literal: When Dun rose in rebellion, Emperor Ming asked Zhan what plan should be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rebelled, Emperor Ming asked Zhan what to do.

sentences.zh: 詹厲然慷慨曰：「陛下宜奮赫斯之威，臣等當得負戈前驅，庶憑宗廟之靈，有征無戰。

translations.literal: Zhan answered sternly and with passion, saying, “Your Majesty ought to rouse the awe-inspiring majesty of a true sovereign; your servants will then be able to bear arms and ride in the van, and perhaps, trusting in the spirits of the ancestral temple, there will be campaigns without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan answered sharply: “You must summon the decisive wrath of a Son of Heaven; we will bear spears in the van, and with the aid of the ancestral spirits we may yet win without a fight.

sentences.zh: 如其不然，王室必危。

translations.literal: If it is not so, the royal house is sure to be imperiled.
translations.idiomatic: If not, the house of Jin will be in grave danger.”

sentences.zh: 」帝以詹爲都督前鋒軍事、護軍將軍、假節，都督朱雀橋南。

translations.literal: ” The emperor made Zhan commander of the vanguard forces, General Who Guards the Army, with credential staff, and put him in overall charge south of the Zhuque Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named him commander of the forward army, General Who Guards the Army, gave him the credential staff, and assigned him the defense south of the Zhuque Bridge.

sentences.zh: 賊從竹格渡江，詹與建威將軍趙胤等擊敗之，斬賊率杜發，梟首數千級。

translations.literal: The rebels crossed the Yangzi at Zhuge Ford; Zhan, together with General Who Establishes Might Zhao Yin and others, defeated them, beheading their leader Du Fa and displaying several thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels forded at Bamboo Lattice; Zhan and Zhao Yin, General Who Establishes Might, smashed them, beheading their chief Du Fa and piling up thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 賊平，封觀陽縣侯，食邑一千六百戶，賜絹五千匹。

translations.literal: When the rebels were crushed, he was enfeoffed as marquis of Guanyang with a fief of 1,600 households and a gift of 5,000 bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory he was made marquis of Guanyang with sixteen hundred taxable households and five thousand rolls of silk.

sentences.zh: 上疏讓曰：「臣聞開國承家，光啟土宇，唯令德元功乃宜封錫。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial declining, saying, “I have heard that when a state is founded and a house continued, and territory is opened in glory, only men of commanding virtue and paramount merit are fit for investiture.
translations.idiomatic: He begged off in a memorial: “I have heard that fiefs belong only to men of shining virtue and supreme merit.

sentences.zh: 臣雖忝當一隊，策無微略，勞不汗馬。

translations.literal: Although I have disgraced myself by leading a single column, my plans were not the least bit subtle, nor did I sweat the horses in toil.
translations.idiomatic: I have merely commanded a unit; I offered no clever strategy and did not exhaust myself in the saddle.

sentences.zh: 猥以疏賤，倫亞親密，暫廁被練，列勤司勳。

translations.literal: Meanly, of base and distant station, I was ranked among the intimate favorites; for a short time I stood in armor among those who labored before the Bureau of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: I am lowborn and remote from court, yet I was classed with the inner circle; I briefly wore armor and was listed among those commended to the ministry of merit.

sentences.zh: 乞迴謬恩，聽其所守。

translations.literal: I beg to have this misplaced favor reversed and to be allowed to hold to what I can guard.”
translations.idiomatic: I ask you to withdraw this undeserved grace and let me keep only what my station warrants.”

sentences.zh: 」不許。

translations.literal: The court did not grant his request.
translations.idiomatic: The throne refused.

sentences.zh: 遷使持節、都督江州諸軍事、平南將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Jiang Province, General Who Pacifies the South, and Inspector of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to bearer of the credential staff, area commander for Jiang province, General Who Pacifies the South, and inspector of Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 詹將行，上疏曰：

translations.literal: As Zhan was about to depart, he submitted a memorial, saying,
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of his departure he presented a memorial:

sentences.zh: 夫欲用天下之智力者，莫若使天下信之也。

translations.literal: If one wishes to employ the intelligence and strength of all the world, nothing equals making the world trust you.
translations.idiomatic: To harness the wit and labor of the empire, nothing works better than earning its trust.

sentences.zh: 商鞅移木，豈禮也哉？

translations.literal: When Shang Yang moved the wooden pole, was that ritual? Yet there was a reason for it.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Yang’s pole-moving trick was hardly orthodox ritual—yet it had its purpose.

sentences.zh: 有由而然。

translations.literal: There was a reason it was so.
translations.idiomatic: It answered a real need.

sentences.zh: 自經荒弊，綱紀穨陵，清直之風既澆，糟秕之俗猶在，誠宜濯以滄浪之流，漉以吞舟之網，則幽顯明別，於變時雍矣。

translations.literal: Since the bonds of order have collapsed in long disorder, the wind of incorruptibility has been washed away while the dregs of lax custom remain; truly we should rinse them in the waters of the Canglang and strain them with a net that swallows boats—then hidden and manifest will be clearly distinguished, and the age will turn harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: After years of ruin the statutes lie in ruins: integrity has thinned while slack habits linger. Wash them in the Canglang’s current and sift them with a net meant for leviathans—then dark and light will sort themselves and the realm will turn toward peace.

sentences.zh: 弘濟茲務，在乎官人。

translations.literal: To enlarge and sustain this task lies in choosing the right officials.
translations.idiomatic: Carrying this through depends on appointing the right men.

sentences.zh: 今南北雜錯，屬託者無保負之累，而輕舉所知，此博采所以未精，職理所以多闕。

translations.literal: Now north and south are jumbled together; those who pull strings bear no liability for failure, yet lightly recommend whoever they know—this is why broad recruitment still misses the mark and why so many offices lack fit incumbents.
translations.idiomatic: North and south are mixed; patrons risk nothing when their picks fail, yet freely tout acquaintances—so wide search still yields mediocrity and posts stay mismatched.

sentences.zh: 今凡有所用，宜隨其能否而與舉主同乎褒貶，則人有慎舉之恭，官無廢職之吝。

translations.literal: Whenever anyone is now employed, let praise and blame fall on the recommender according to the appointee’s competence; then men will be cautious whom they advance, and offices will not suffer the shame of vacant duty.
translations.idiomatic: Tie every appointment to the sponsor’s own record of praise or blame, and recommenders will tread carefully while no post sits idle.

sentences.zh: 昔冀缺有功，胥臣蒙先茅之賞；

translations.literal: In antiquity, when Ji Que achieved merit, Xu Chen received the reward of the vanguard’s plumes;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Ji Que earned distinction, Xu Chen shared the honor of the first pennant;

sentences.zh: 子玉敗軍，子文受蔿賈之責。

translations.literal: when Ziyu’s army was defeated, Ziwen bore the reproach of Wei Jia.
translations.idiomatic: when Ziyu lost his army, Ziwen took Wei Jia’s rebuke.

sentences.zh: 古既有之，今亦宜然。

translations.literal: The ancients had such precedents; today we should do likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients set this pattern; we should follow it now.

sentences.zh: 漢朝使刺史行部，乘傳奏事，猶恐不足以辨彰幽明，弘宣政道，故復有繡衣直指。

translations.literal: In Han, when the regional inspectors made their rounds, riding the post relays to report affairs, they still feared this was not enough to distinguish the hidden from the manifest and spread the royal way—so there were also the silk-robed direct investigators.
translations.idiomatic: Han’s provincial inspectors toured by relay yet still worried they could not lay bare truth from falsehood or broadcast policy—hence the silk-clad special envoys.

sentences.zh: 今之艱弊，過於往昔，宜分遣黃、散若中書郎等循行天下，觀採得失，舉善彈違，斷截苟且，則人不敢爲非矣。

translations.literal: Today’s hardships exceed those times; it would be right to dispatch Yellow Gate and Scattered Cavalier attendants, or gentlemen of the secretariat, to travel the realm, observe gains and losses, promote the good and impeach the wicked, and cut off corner-cutting—then men would not dare to do wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Our troubles are worse; we should send out yellow-gate and scattered cavalry attendants, or secretariat gentlemen, to circuit the empire, gather what works and what fails, lift the worthy and strike the corrupt, and end shoddy shortcuts—so no one dares misconduct.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝時，二千石有居職修明者，則入爲公卿；

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuan of Han, when a commandery governor of two thousand piculs held office with clear achievement, he was promoted into the ranks of dukes and ministers;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan of Han found a two-thousand-picul magistrate diligent in office, he moved him straight into the highest council;

sentences.zh: 其不稱職免官者，皆還爲平人。

translations.literal: those who proved unfit were dismissed and returned to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: those who failed were cashiered back to private life.

sentences.zh: 懲勸必行，故歷世長久。

translations.literal: Because reward and punishment were sure to be enforced, the dynasty endured for ages.
translations.idiomatic: Because incentives and sanctions were real, the dynasty lasted.

sentences.zh: 中間以來，遷不足競，免不足懼。

translations.literal: From the middle period onward, promotion is not worth striving for and dismissal is not worth fearing.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages made promotion hardly worth chasing and demotion hardly worth dreading.

sentences.zh: 或有進而失意，退而得分。

translations.literal: Some advance yet lose favor, while others retire yet gain advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Some rise and still fall from grace; others step down yet profit.

sentences.zh: 蒞官雖美，當以素論降替；

translations.literal: Though the office one assumes may be splendid, demotion should follow plain public verdict;
translations.idiomatic: Even a handsome appointment should be lowered when general opinion turns;

sentences.zh: 在職實劣，直以舊望登敘。

translations.literal: those who are truly incompetent in office are advanced in order purely by old reputation.
translations.idiomatic: men who plainly fail in post climb the ladder on stale prestige alone.

sentences.zh: 校游談爲多少，不以實事爲先後。

translations.literal: They tally idle talk instead of weighing real deeds.
translations.idiomatic: People count reputations for clever chatter rather than real performance.

sentences.zh: 以此責成，臣未見其兆也。

translations.literal: If we demand success on this basis, I have yet to see the sign of it.
translations.idiomatic: Expect good government from that, and I see no portent of it.

sentences.zh: 今宜峻左降舊制，可二千石免官，三年乃得敘用，長史六年，戶口折半，道里倍之。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to tighten the old rules of demotion: let a dismissed two-thousand-picul official wait three years before reinstatement, a chief clerk six years, halving the household quota and doubling the mileage requirement.
translations.idiomatic: Tighten the classical demotion code: make a cashiered two-thousand-picul magistrate wait three years before reuse, a chief clerk six, cut registered households by half, and double the distance rule.

sentences.zh: 此法必明，使天下知官難得而易失，必人慎其職，朝無惰官矣。

translations.literal: If this law is made clear, the realm will know offices are hard to win and easy to lose; men will be careful in their duties, and the court will have no lazy officials.
translations.idiomatic: Spell that out so everyone knows rank is scarce and fragile; officers will guard their posts and the court will shed slackers.

sentences.zh: 都督可課佃二十頃，州十頃，郡五頃，縣三頃。

translations.literal: Area commanders may be allotted twenty qing of tenant land, prefectures ten, commanderies five, counties three.
translations.idiomatic: Let area commanders farm twenty qing of allotted fields, prefects ten, magistrates of commanderies five, county magistrates three.

sentences.zh: 皆取文武吏醫卜，不得撓亂百姓。

translations.literal: All such labor should draw only clerks, physicians, and diviners, and must not harass the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Man them solely with civil clerks, doctors, and soothsayers—never press ordinary households.

sentences.zh: 三臺九府，中外諸軍，有可減損，皆令附農。

translations.literal: The Three Platforms, the Nine Bureaus, inner and outer armies—wherever cuts can be made, order them attached to agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Every office from the three platforms and nine ministries down to central and field armies should trim superfluous posts and put freed hands to farming.

sentences.zh: 市息末伎，道無游人，不過一熟，豐穰可必。

translations.literal: Let markets quiet petty crafts until no idler wanders the roads; before a single harvest passes, abundance can be assured.
translations.idiomatic: Still the markets’ petty trades until the roads hold no drifters; one good season will bring plenty.

sentences.zh: 然後重居職之俸，使祿足以代耕。

translations.literal: Then increase the salary of those who hold substantive posts, so that stipends truly replace plowing.
translations.idiomatic: Then raise salaries for substantive posts so emoluments truly replace tilling the soil.

sentences.zh: 頃大事之後，遐邇皆想宏略，而寂然未副，宜早振綱領，肅起群望。

translations.literal: After the recent great upheaval, near and far alike looked for a grand design, yet silence has not matched expectation; the net of government should be tightened early to rouse universal hope.
translations.idiomatic: After the great convulsion everyone expects bold leadership, yet little has changed; pull the reins tight now to answer that hope.

sentences.zh: 時王敦新平，人情未安，詹撫而懷之，莫不得其歡心，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Dun had just been crushed; hearts were not yet settled; Zhan comforted and cherished the people, and none failed to give him their goodwill—the common folk depended on him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun had only just been defeated; nerves were raw. Zhan soothed and won every heart, and the people leaned on him.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，與陶侃書曰：「每憶密計，自沔入湘，頡頏繾綣，齊好斷金。

translations.literal: When his illness grew grave, he wrote to Tao Kan, saying, “Whenever I recall our secret plans, marching from the Mian into the Xiang, soaring together yet bound close as cord, our friendship could sever metal.
translations.idiomatic: As his sickness worsened he wrote Tao Kan: “Each time I remember our hidden strategy, driving from the Han bend into the Xiang, rising side by side yet clinging like lovers, our accord was strong enough to cut metal.”

sentences.zh: 子南我東，忽然一紀，其間事故，何所不有。

translations.literal: You have held the south, I the east; suddenly a full twelve-year cycle has passed, and in that span what event has not occurred?
translations.idiomatic: You have been in the southern theater, I in the east; twelve years have slipped by, and between us everything imaginable has happened.

sentences.zh: 足下建功嶠南，旋鎮舊楚。

translations.literal: Below you have won merit beyond the mountain ranges and then returned to secure old Chu.
translations.idiomatic: You built your merit south of the ranges, then swung back to hold the Chu heartland.

sentences.zh: 吾承乏幸會，來忝此州，圖與足下進共竭節本朝，報恩幼主，退以申尋平生，纏綿舊好。

translations.literal: I, filling a vacancy by happy chance, have come in shame to this province, hoping that with you I might advance together to exhaust our loyalty to the court, repay grace to the young sovereign, and in retirement renew our lifelong ties and the warmth of our old friendship.
translations.idiomatic: I stumbled into this governorship and crossed into your province hoping we could serve the throne side by side, repay the boy emperor’s trust, and in quieter days pick up the friendship we began long ago.

sentences.zh: 豈悟時不我與，長即幽冥，永言莫從，能不慨悵！

translations.literal: Who would have thought the times would not favor us, and that I would soon pass into the dark world, so that my words can never reach you—how can I not feel grief and regret!
translations.idiomatic: Yet time turned against us: I am slipping into the shades and can no longer reach you—how could I not ache with regret?

sentences.zh: 今神州未夷，四方多難，足下年德並隆，功名俱盛，宜務建洪範，雖休勿休，至公至平，至謙至順，即自天祐之，吉無不利。

translations.literal: Now the heartland is not yet pacified and troubles press on every side; your years and virtue stand together at their height, and fame and achievement are both at their peak. You ought to strive to enact the great model: though there be rest, do not rest; be utterly fair, utterly even, utterly humble, utterly compliant—then Heaven itself will bless you, and good fortune will know no ill.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plain is still in turmoil. You are at the peak of age, virtue, name, and deed; you should live out the Great Plan—never slacken though the moment seems calm; hold to perfect equity, humility, and deference, and Heaven will shelter you with unbroken good fortune.

sentences.zh: 人之將死，其言也善，足下察吾此誠。

translations.literal: When a man is about to die, his words are kindly; I pray you discern the sincerity in what I say.
translations.idiomatic: A dying man’s words are meant kindly—please read my heart in them.”

sentences.zh: 」以咸和六年卒，[1]時年五十三。

translations.literal: ” He died in the sixth year of Xianhe, at age fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 331, the sixth year of Xianhe, aged fifty-three.”

sentences.zh: 冊贈鎮南大將軍、儀同三司，諡曰烈，祠以太牢。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored by patent as General Who Guards the South and granted the Three Offices parity of ceremony; his posthumous name was “Stalwart,” and he received sacrifice with the grand victim.
translations.idiomatic: The court issued a patent posthumously naming him General Who Guards the South with three-offices protocol, styled him “Stalwart,” and offered him the great beast sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 子玄嗣，位至散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Xuan succeeded him and rose to Gentleman Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Ying Xuan rose to gentleman cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 玄弟誕，有器榦，歷六郡太守、龍驤將軍，追贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuan’s younger brother Dan had capacity and backbone; he served as administrator of six commanderies and as General Who Inspires Might, and was posthumously awarded the title Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Ying Dan was capable and forceful, served as magistrate over six commanderies and as General Who Inspires Might, and was posthumously named inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 初，京兆韋泓喪亂之際，親屬遇饑疫並盡，客遊洛陽，素聞詹名，遂依託之。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the convulsions of the age, Wei Hong of Jingzhao lost every kinsman to famine and plague; as a client traveler in Luoyang he had long heard Zhan’s name and therefore attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei Hong of Jingzhao had seen his whole family die in famine and plague; stranded in Luoyang he had heard of Ying Zhan and threw in his lot with him.

sentences.zh: 詹與分甘共苦，情若弟兄。

translations.literal: Zhan shared sweets and bitterness with him; their feelings were like those of elder and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan shared every hardship with him as though they were brothers.

sentences.zh: 遂隨從積年，爲營伉儷，置居宅，并薦之於元帝曰：「自遭喪亂，人士易操，至乃任運固窮，耿介守節者尟矣。

translations.literal: He followed him for accumulated years; Zhan arranged a marriage for him, set up a residence, and moreover recommended him to Emperor Yuan, saying, “Since the disasters began, scholars have easily shifted their conduct; as for those who accept fate and cling to poverty, who stand aloof and keep their integrity—such are few.
translations.idiomatic: For years Hong followed him; Zhan found him a wife, a house, and urged him on the emperor: “Since the collapse, men change their colors; those who accept poverty and keep their integrity intact are rare.

sentences.zh: 伏見議郎韋泓，年三十八，字元量，執心清沖，才識備濟，躬耕隴畝，不煩人役，靜默居常，不豫政事。

translations.literal: I have seen Consultant Hong, thirty-eight sui, courtesy name Yuanliang, whose mind is pure and limpid, whose talent and judgment are fully rounded; he personally plows the fields, troubling no one for labor, and dwells in quiet retirement, not meddling in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I present Consultant Wei Hong, thirty-eight, style Yuanliang—clear in purpose, ample in ability, tills his own fields, keeps to himself, and never meddles in politics.

sentences.zh: 昔年流移，來在詹境，經寇喪資，一身特立，短褐不掩形，菜蔬不充朝，而抗志彌厲，不遊非類。

translations.literal: In former years, drifting in flight, he came into the territory I govern; he passed through banditry and lost his goods, yet stands alone; a short coat does not cover his body, vegetables do not fill his morning meal, yet his high purpose grows only sterner, and he does not consort with unworthy sorts.
translations.idiomatic: He fled into my jurisdiction, was robbed of everything, yet stands alone in a coat too short to cover him, on a diet of greens, his resolve only harder, keeping clear of the wrong crowd.

sentences.zh: 顏回稱不改其樂，泓有其分。

translations.literal: Yan Hui spoke of not altering his joy; Hong has his share of that.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Hui spoke of joy unchanged by poverty; Hong has earned the same praise.

sentences.zh: 明公輔亮皇室，恢維宇宙，四門開闢，英彥鳧藻，收春華於京輦，採秋實於巖藪。

translations.literal: The enlightened lord assists and illumines the royal house, restores order within the four seas; the four gates stand open, and worthy men flock like waterfowl and water-plants; you gather spring blossoms at the capital chariots and harvest autumn fruit from mountain and marsh.
translations.idiomatic: You steady the throne and set the cosmos aright; the gates are open and talent swarms in—you gather spring blossoms at court and autumn fruit from the wilds.

sentences.zh: 而泓抱璞荊山，未剖和璧。

translations.literal: Yet Hong clasps the jade at Mount Jing, the He shi disk still uncut.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hong still clutches his jade on Mount Jing, the flawless stone uncut.

sentences.zh: 若蒙銓召，付以列曹，必能協隆鼎味，緝熙庶績者也。

translations.literal: If you would deign to summon and assign him to one of the bureaus, he is sure to be able to harmonize the flavor of the cauldron and bring bright order to the myriad tasks.”
translations.idiomatic: If you call him into a ministry, he will season the state’s stew and bring luster to every task.”

sentences.zh: 」帝即辟之。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him at once.

sentences.zh: 自後位至少府卿。

translations.literal: Afterward he rose to Junior Minister of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually became junior minister of the palace.

sentences.zh: 既受詹生成之惠，詹卒，遂製朋友之服，哭止宿草，追趙氏祀程嬰、杵臼之義，祭詹終身。

translations.literal: Having received from Zhan the kindness that gave him life, when Zhan died he therefore assumed the mourning garments of a friend, weeping until the grass on the grave had ceased its yearly growth; emulating the righteousness of Cheng Ying and the pestle-bearer in the Zhao orphan tale, he sacrificed to Zhan for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan had raised him like a second birth; when Zhan died he wore a friend’s mourning, wept the full year at the grave, and for life afterward offered sacrifice, modeling himself on Cheng Ying and Gongsun Chujiu.

sentences.zh: 甘卓字季思，丹楊人，秦丞相茂之後也。

translations.literal: Gan Zhuo, courtesy name Jisi, was a native of Danyang and a descendant of Gan Mao, Chancellor of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo, style Jisi, came from Danyang and traced his line to Gan Mao, Qin’s chancellor.

sentences.zh: 曾祖寧，爲吳將。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ning was a general of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gan Ning had been a Wu general.

sentences.zh: 祖述，仕吳爲尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shu served Wu as Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gan Shu served Wu as palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 父昌，太子太傅。

translations.literal: His father Chang was Junior Tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gan Chang was junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 吳平，卓退居自守。

translations.literal: When Wu was pacified, Zhuo withdrew and kept to himself.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell, Zhuo retired and lived quietly.

sentences.zh: 郡命主簿、功曹，察孝廉，州舉秀才，爲吳王常侍。

translations.literal: The commandery appointed him chief clerk and merit assessor; he was recommended as filially devout and incorrupt, the province raised him as cultivated talent, and he became attendant to the Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery named him chief clerk and merit assessor; he earned filial-incorrupt recommendation, the province put him forward as cultivated talent, and he became attendant to the prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 討石冰，以功賜爵都亭侯。

translations.literal: He campaigned against Shi Bing and, for merit, was enfeoffed as village marquis of Duting.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in crushing Shi Bing he received the village marquisate of Duting.

sentences.zh: 東海王越引爲參軍，出補離狐令。

translations.literal: Prince Sima Yue of the East Sea took him on as a staff adviser and sent him out to fill the vacancy as magistrate of Lihu.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue of the East Sea enlisted him as adviser and sent him out as magistrate of Lihu.

sentences.zh: 卓見天下大亂，棄官東歸，前至歷陽，與陳敏相遇。

translations.literal: Zhuo saw that the realm was in great turmoil, resigned his office, and returned east; when he reached Liyang he met Chen Min.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing chaos everywhere, he quit his post and headed east; at Liyang he ran into Chen Min.

sentences.zh: 敏甚悅，共圖縱橫之計，遂爲其子景娶卓女，共相結託。

translations.literal: Min was greatly pleased; together they plotted a strategy of maneuvering among the powers, whereupon Min took Zhuo’s daughter as wife for his son Jing, and they bound themselves to each other in mutual reliance.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min was delighted; they laid plans to play the powers against each other, Chen Min married Zhuo’s daughter to his son Chen Jing, and the two families hitched their fortunes together.

sentences.zh: 會周玘唱義，密使錢廣攻敏弟昶，敏遣卓討廣，頓朱雀橋南。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhou Qi raised the standard of righteousness and secretly sent Qian Guang to attack Min’s younger brother Chang; Min dispatched Zhuo to campaign against Guang, halting south of the Zhuque Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Qi raised loyal troops and secretly sent Qian Guang against Chen Min’s brother Chang, Chen Min ordered Zhuo to attack Qian Guang and camped south of the Zhuque Bridge.

sentences.zh: 會廣殺昶，玘告丹楊太守顧榮共邀說卓。

translations.literal: It happened that Guang killed Chang, and Qi informed Grand Administrator Gu Rong of Danyang to join in inviting and persuading Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Guang killed Chang, Zhou Qi told Gu Rong, grand administrator of Danyang, to help win Zhuo over.

sentences.zh: 卓素敬服榮，且以昶死懷懼，良久乃從之。

translations.literal: Zhuo had always revered Rong, and moreover, with Chang’s death, felt fear; only after a long while did he consent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo respected Gu Rong deeply and, with Chang dead, was afraid; only after long hesitation did he agree.

sentences.zh: 遂詐疾迎女，斷橋，收船南岸，共滅敏，傳首于京都。

translations.literal: Thereupon he feigned illness to fetch his daughter back, broke the bridge, gathered boats on the south bank, and together they destroyed Min, sending his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He pretended illness to fetch his daughter home, cut the bridge, massed boats on the south bank, joined in destroying Chen Min, and sent the rebel’s head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 元帝初渡江，授卓前鋒都督、揚威將軍、歷陽內史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan first crossed the Yangzi, he appointed Zhuo commander of the vanguard, General Who Displays Might, and interior minister of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan first crossed the river, he made Zhuo vanguard commander, General Who Displays Might, and interior minister of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 其後討周馥，征杜弢，屢經苦戰，多所擒獲。

translations.literal: Afterward he campaigned against Zhou Fu and against Du Tao, repeatedly fighting hard battles and taking many captives.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fought Zhou Fu and Du Tao, endured bitter fighting, and took many prisoners.

sentences.zh: 以前後功，進爵南鄉侯，拜豫章太守。

translations.literal: For merit accumulated before and after, he was advanced in rank to marquis of Nanxiang and appointed grand administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: For successive victories he was promoted to marquis of Nanxiang and grand administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 尋遷湘州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Inspector of Xiang Province, keeping his general’s title as before.
translations.idiomatic: He soon moved to inspector of Xiang while keeping his generalcy.

sentences.zh: 復進爵于湖侯。

translations.literal: His fief was again raised to marquis of Yuhu.
translations.idiomatic: His marquisate was advanced again to Yuhu.

sentences.zh: 中興初，以邊寇未靜，學校陵遲，特聽不試孝廉，而秀才猶依舊策試。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Restoration, because border raiders were not yet quiet and schools were in decline, the court specially permitted filial-incorrupt candidates to skip the examination, while cultivated talents still underwent the old policy examination.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Eastern Jin revival, border raiders kept schools disrupted, so filial-incorrupt nominees were excused from exams while cultivated talents still faced the written policy test.

sentences.zh: 卓上疏以爲：「答問損益，當須博通古今，明達政體，必求諸墳索，乃堪其舉。

translations.literal: Zhuo submitted a memorial arguing that “to answer questions on profit and harm requires broad mastery of past and present and clear understanding of government; one must seek learning in the tomes of the classics to be fit for recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo argued in a memorial that policy essays demand wide learning and political sense, and only men grounded in the classics should sit for them.

sentences.zh: 臣所忝州往遭寇亂，學校久替，人士流播，不得比之餘州。

translations.literal: The province over which I have the dishonor to preside has lately suffered invasion and turmoil; its schools have long decayed, and its gentlemen have scattered in flight—it cannot be compared with other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: My province has been ravaged; its schools are ruined and its scholars scattered—it cannot match other regions.

sentences.zh: 策試之由，當藉學功，謂宜同孝廉例，申與期限。

translations.literal: The reason for policy examination ought to rest on scholarly achievement; I say it should follow the filial-incorrupt precedent and be granted an extension of time.”
translations.idiomatic: Testing should wait on real schooling; grant cultivated talents the same extension already given filial-incorrupt nominees.”

sentences.zh: 」疏奏，朝議不許。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, court discussion did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated his plea and refused it.

sentences.zh: 卓於是精加隱括，備禮舉桂陽谷儉爲秀才。

translations.literal: Zhuo therefore scrutinized candidates with care, performed the full rites, and recommended Gu Jian of Guiyang as cultivated talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo combed his commandery with care, observed every courtesy, and nominated Gu Jian of Guiyang as cultivated talent.

sentences.zh: 儉辭不獲命，州厚禮遣之。

translations.literal: Jian declined but could not escape the order; the province sent him off with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Jian tried to decline but could not; the province lavished gifts and dispatched him.

sentences.zh: 諸州秀才聞當考試，皆憚不行，惟儉一人到臺，遂不復策試。

translations.literal: When the cultivated talents of the various provinces heard they would be examined, all feared to go; only Jian alone arrived at the ministry, so in the end no policy examination was held.
translations.idiomatic: Word of the exam frightened every province’s nominees away—only Gu Jian appeared at the ministry, so the court dropped the test entirely.

sentences.zh: 儉恥其州少士，乃表求試，以高第除中郎。

translations.literal: Jian was ashamed that his province had so few scholars; he therefore petitioned to be examined and, with high marks, was appointed gentleman of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of his province’s thin bench, Gu Jian begged to sit the exam, scored at the top, and was named a gentleman of the palace.

sentences.zh: 儉少有志行，寒苦自立，博涉經史。

translations.literal: Jian in youth had determination and conduct; in cold hardship he established himself and read widely in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Jian had resolve even as a youth; he pulled himself up in poverty and read widely in classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 于時南土凋荒，經籍道息，儉不能遠求師友，唯在家研精。

translations.literal: At that time the southern lands were wasted and barren, and the transmission of texts had ceased; Jian could not seek teachers or friends at a distance, and could only refine his studies at home.
translations.idiomatic: The south was barren and books scarce; he could not travel for teachers and had to grind away alone at home.

sentences.zh: 雖所得實深，未有名譽，又恥衒耀取達，遂歸，終身不仕，卒于家。

translations.literal: Although what he gained was truly deep, he had not yet won reputation, and he was ashamed to vaunt himself to advance; he therefore returned home, never took office all his life, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: His learning ran deep yet brought no fame, and he scorned self-advertisement; he went home, never served, and died there.

sentences.zh: 卓尋遷安南將軍、梁州刺史、假節、督沔北諸軍，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Zhuo soon was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Liang Province, with credential staff, commanding all armies north of the Mian, and stationed at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was soon raised to General Who Pacifies the South, inspector of Liang, with staff of authority over the forces north of the Han, based at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 卓外柔內剛，爲政簡惠，善於綏撫，估稅悉除，市無二價。

translations.literal: Zhuo was outwardly yielding yet inwardly firm; his government was simple and beneficent, and he was skilled in soothing and comforting; market tolls were all abolished, and in the markets there were not two prices.
translations.idiomatic: He seemed soft outside but was steel within; his rule was lean and kind, superb at pacification—he abolished market surcharges so a single price prevailed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 州境所有魚池，先恒責稅，卓不收其利，皆給貧民，西土稱爲惠政。

translations.literal: All fishponds within the province had constantly been subject to tax; Zhuo did not take their profit but assigned it all to the poor, and the western lands praised it as a benevolent policy.
translations.idiomatic: Fishponds once taxed for revenue he threw open to the poor, and the west hailed it as merciful rule.

sentences.zh: 王敦稱兵，遣使告卓。

translations.literal: Wang Dun raised troops and sent a messenger to inform Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun rebelled he sent word to Gan Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓乃僞許，而心不同之。

translations.literal: Zhuo therefore feigned consent, but in his heart did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo pretended assent while inwardly refusing.

sentences.zh: 及敦升舟，而卓不赴，使參軍孫雙詣武昌諫止敦。

translations.literal: When Dun embarked his fleet, Zhuo did not join him; he sent his staff adviser Sun Shuang to Wuchang to remonstrate with Dun and stop him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun’s fleet sailed, Zhuo stayed away and sent adviser Sun Shuang to Wuchang to block him.

sentences.zh: 敦聞雙言，大驚曰：「甘侯前與吾語云何，而更有異！

translations.literal: When Dun heard Shuang’s words he was greatly startled and said, “What did Lord Gan say to me before, that he should now change!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun was stunned: “What did Lord Gan promise me earlier, that he should shift so?”

sentences.zh: 正當慮吾危朝廷邪？

translations.literal: Surely he only worries that I endanger the court?”
translations.idiomatic: Does he think I mean to harm the throne?”

sentences.zh: 吾今下唯除姦凶耳。

translations.literal: Now that I am descending, it is only to remove the wicked.”
translations.idiomatic: I am coming downriver solely to purge traitors.”

sentences.zh: 卿還言之，事濟當以甘侯作公。

translations.literal: Return and tell him: when the affair succeeds, I shall make Lord Gan a duke.”
translations.idiomatic: Go back and say that when this is done Lord Gan will be made a duke.”

sentences.zh: 」雙還報卓，卓不能決。

translations.literal: ” Shuang returned and reported to Zhuo, yet Zhuo could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shuang reported back, but Zhuo still could not choose a side.

sentences.zh: 或說卓且僞許敦，待敦至都而討之。

translations.literal: Some urged Zhuo for the moment to pretend to obey Dun, then strike him after he reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Some said: feign obedience, then ambush Wang Dun once he reaches the capital.

sentences.zh: 卓曰：「昔陳敏之亂，吾亦先從後圖，而論者謂懼逼而謀之。

translations.literal: Zhuo said, “In the Chen Min rebellion I also first followed and later plotted, and critics said I acted from fear of pressure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo said, “During Chen Min’s revolt I first went along and only later turned—people said I moved from fear.

sentences.zh: 雖吾情本不爾，而事實有似，心恒愧之。

translations.literal: Although in my heart it was not so, the facts looked similar, and I have always felt ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: My motives were not that base, yet it looked the same, and the memory shames me.

sentences.zh: 今若復爾，誰能明我！

translations.literal: If I did the same again, who could make my sincerity clear!”
translations.idiomatic: If I repeat that performance, who will believe my good faith?”

sentences.zh: 」時湘州刺史譙王承遣主簿鄧騫說卓曰：「劉大連雖乘權寵，非有害於天下也。

translations.literal: ” At that time Prince Sima Cheng of Qiao, Inspector of Xiang Province, sent his chief clerk Deng Qian to persuade Zhuo, saying, “Liu Dalian, though riding on favor and power, does no harm to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Prince Sima Cheng of Qiao, inspector of Xiang, sent Deng Qian to argue: “Liu Kui may cling to favor, but he does not injure the state.

sentences.zh: 大將軍以其私憾稱兵象魏，雖託討亂之名，實失天下之望，此忠臣義士匡救之時也。

translations.literal: The grand general, nursing a private grudge, has raised troops at the capital; though he claims the name of punishing rebels, in truth he has forfeited the hopes of the realm—this is the hour for loyal ministers and righteous knights to set things right.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general marches on a private vendetta; though he calls it a punitive campaign, he has lost the world’s trust—this is the moment for loyal men to act.

sentences.zh: 昔魯連匹夫，猶懷蹈海之志，況受任方伯，位同體國者乎！

translations.literal: In old days Lu Zhonglian was a mere commoner, yet he cherished the resolve to leap into the sea; how much more one who holds a regional command and shares one body with the state!”
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhonglian was only a private man yet would drown for principle—how much more a regional commander whose fate is the dynasty’s!”

sentences.zh: 今若因天人之心，唱桓文之舉，杖大順以掃逆節，擁義兵以勤王室，斯千載之運，不可失也。

translations.literal: Now if you seize the hearts of Heaven and men, raise the banner of Huan and Wen, wield the great compliance to sweep away rebellion, and gather righteous troops to aid the royal house, it is a fortune of a thousand ages—do not let it slip.”
translations.idiomatic: Seize heaven and earth’s mood, take up the mantle of Duke Huan and Duke Wen, march under the great mandate to crush treason, and rally loyal armies for the throne—a chance like this comes once in an age.”

sentences.zh: 」卓笑曰：「桓文之事，豈吾所能。

translations.literal: Zhuo smiled and said, “The deeds of Huan and Wen—how could I be capable of them?
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo smiled: “The achievements of Huan and Wen are beyond me.

sentences.zh: 至於盡力國難，乃其心也。

translations.literal: As for exhausting my strength on the state’s peril, that is indeed my heart.”
translations.idiomatic: Still, to throw my whole strength into the kingdom’s crisis—that I mean to do.”

sentences.zh: 當共詳思之。

translations.literal: We ought together to deliberate it carefully.”
translations.idiomatic: We must think this through together.”

sentences.zh: 」參軍李梁說卓曰：「昔隗囂亂隴右，竇融保河西以歸光武，今日之事，有似於此。

translations.literal: ” Staff adviser Li Liang said to Zhuo, “In old days Wei Xiao threw Longyou into turmoil, while Dou Rong held Hexi and submitted to Guangwu; today’s affair is somewhat like that.
translations.idiomatic: His adviser Li Liang said, “Wei Xiao once tore Longyou apart while Dou Rong held Hexi for Guangwu—today resembles that.

sentences.zh: 將軍有重名於天下，但當推亡固存，坐而待之。

translations.literal: The general enjoys a weighty name in the realm; you need only let the doomed perish and secure what survives, sitting and awaiting the outcome.
translations.idiomatic: You are famous everywhere; let the losing side fall and the winning rise while you wait.

sentences.zh: 使大將軍勝，方當崇將軍以方面之重；

translations.literal: If the grand general wins, he will surely honor the general with a heavy frontier commission;
translations.idiomatic: If the grand general wins, he will ennoble you with a great border command;

sentences.zh: 如其不勝，朝廷必以將軍代之。

translations.literal: if he does not win, the court is sure to replace him with the general.
translations.idiomatic: if he loses, the court will put you in his place.

sentences.zh: 何憂不富貴，而釋此廟勝，決存亡於一戰邪！

translations.literal: Why worry that you will not be rich and noble, yet abandon this council-hall strategy and stake survival on a single battle!”
translations.idiomatic: Why trade a sure path to wealth for one desperate battle?”

sentences.zh: 」騫謂梁曰：「光武創業，中國未平，故隗囂斷隴右，竇融兼河西，各據一方，鼎足之勢，故得文服天子，從容顧望。

translations.literal: Qian said to Liang, “When Guangwu founded his enterprise, the central plain was not yet pacified; therefore Wei Xiao cut off Longyou and Dou Rong held Hexi, each occupying a corner in a tripod stance, and so could pay court in civil dress while leisurely watching how things tilted.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qian retorted: “When Guangwu began, the heartland was still unsettled, so Wei Xiao blocked Longyou and Dou Rong held Hexi—each corner of a tripod could bow from afar and watch the wind.

sentences.zh: 及海內已定，君臣正位，終於隴右傾覆，河西入朝。

translations.literal: Once the realm within the seas was settled and ruler and minister took their proper places, in the end Longyou collapsed and Hexi entered the court.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empire was fixed and ruler and ministers stood straight, Longyou fell and Hexi came in.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why was that?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 向之文服，義所不容也。

translations.literal: Because the earlier show of civil submission was something righteousness could not tolerate.
translations.idiomatic: Because feigned submission could not forever satisfy duty.

sentences.zh: 今將軍之於本朝，非竇融之喻也。

translations.literal: Now the general’s relation to this court is not comparable to Dou Rong’s case.
translations.idiomatic: You are no Dou Rong toward this court.

sentences.zh: 襄陽之於大府，非河西之固也。

translations.literal: Xiangyang’s relation to the great headquarters is not as secure as Hexi was.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang is not the fortress Hexi was.

sentences.zh: 且人臣之義，安忍國難而不陳力，何以北面於天子邪！

translations.literal: Moreover, in the duty of a subject, how can one endure the state’s peril without offering one’s strength—by what right face the Son of Heaven to the north!”
translations.idiomatic: How can a minister watch the throne in danger and offer nothing, then claim to face the emperor?”

sentences.zh: 使大將軍平劉隗，還武昌，增石城之守，絕荊湘之粟，將軍安歸乎？

translations.literal: Suppose the grand general crushes Liu Kui, returns to Wuchang, strengthens the garrison at Stone City, and cuts the grain of Jing and Xiang—where will the general go then?
translations.idiomatic: If Wang Dun beats Liu Kui, returns to Wuchang, fortifies Stone City, and chokes off Jing and Xiang grain, where will you run?

sentences.zh: 勢在人手，而曰我處廟勝，未之聞也。

translations.literal: The advantage lies in another’s hands, yet you say you sit in council-hall victory—I have never heard the like.”
translations.idiomatic: Power sits in his hands while you talk of winning in council—I have never heard such folly.”

sentences.zh: 」卓尚持疑未決，騫又謂卓曰：「今既不義舉，又不承大將軍檄，此必至之禍，愚智所見也。

translations.literal: Zhuo still hesitated undecided; Qian again said to Zhuo, “Now, since you neither raise a righteous host nor accept the grand general’s summons, disaster is sure to follow—a fool and a sage would agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo still wavered; Deng Qian pressed him: “Neither marching nor answering the summons means certain ruin—any fool sees it.

sentences.zh: 且議者之所難，以彼強我弱，是不量虛實者也。

translations.literal: Moreover, what doubters find hard is that he seems strong and we weak—that is failure to measure true strength.
translations.idiomatic: They say he is strong and we weak because they misread the balance.

sentences.zh: 今大將軍兵不過萬餘，其留者不能五千，而將軍見眾既倍之矣。

translations.literal: Now the grand general’s troops are no more than ten thousand odd, and those left behind cannot reach five thousand, while the troops you command are already more than double that.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun has barely ten thousand men, fewer than five thousand left behind, while you command more than twice that host.

sentences.zh: 將軍威名天下所聞也，此府精銳，戰勝之兵也。

translations.literal: The general’s awe-inspiring name is known throughout the realm; these crack troops of the headquarters are soldiers accustomed to victory.
translations.idiomatic: Your name shakes the empire, and these are the capital’s picked veterans.

sentences.zh: 擁強眾，藉威名，杖節而行，豈王含所能御哉！

translations.literal: Bearing a mighty host, relying on a famed name, and marching with the credential staff—how could Wang Han possibly withstand you!
translations.idiomatic: March with your doubled army, your reputation, and the imperial staff—Wang Han cannot hold you.

sentences.zh: 溯流之眾，勢不自救，將軍之舉武昌，若摧枯拉朽，何所顧慮乎！

translations.literal: A host rowing upstream cannot save itself; your strike at Wuchang will be like snapping dry rot—what is there to hesitate over!
translations.idiomatic: His upstream relief cannot save him; you would crush Wuchang like dead wood—why flinch?

sentences.zh: 武昌既定，據其軍實，鎮撫二州，施惠士卒，使還者如歸，此呂蒙所以克敵也。

translations.literal: Once Wuchang is secure, seize its stores, pacify the two provinces, shower favors on the soldiers, and make those who return feel they are coming home—this is how Lü Meng overcame his foe.
translations.idiomatic: Take Wuchang, seize its arsenals, calm two provinces, reward the ranks, and men will flock home—that was Lü Meng’s winning move.

sentences.zh: 如是，大將軍可不戰而自潰。

translations.literal: In that case the grand general may collapse without a battle.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wang Dun may fall without a fight.

sentences.zh: 今釋必勝之策，安坐以待危亡，不可言知計矣。

translations.literal: To cast aside a strategy sure of victory, sit at ease, and await ruin—this cannot be called knowing how to plan.”
translations.idiomatic: To abandon a winning plan and sit waiting for doom is not wisdom.”

sentences.zh: 願將軍熟慮之。」

translations.literal: I beg the general to ponder it carefully.”
translations.idiomatic: Think on it carefully, general.”

sentences.zh: 時敦以卓不至，慮在後爲變，遣參軍樂道融苦要卓俱下。

translations.literal: At that time, because Zhuo had not come, Dun feared he might make trouble in the rear and sent his staff adviser Yue Daorong urgently to insist that Zhuo descend with him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhuo had not joined him, Wang Dun feared trouble from the rear and sent Yue Daorong to drag Gan Zhuo downriver with the fleet.

sentences.zh: 道融本欲背敦，因說卓襲之，語在融傳。

translations.literal: Daorong had originally intended to betray Dun, and therefore urged Zhuo to strike him; the account is given in Daorong’s biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Daorong meant to turn on Wang Dun and urged Gan Zhuo to hit him first—the full story is in Daorong’s biography.

sentences.zh: 卓既素不欲從敦，得道融說，遂決曰：「吾本意也。

translations.literal: Zhuo, who had never wished to follow Dun, once he heard Daorong’s argument, decided and said, “This is my original intent.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo had long resisted Wang Dun; Daorong’s words settled him: “That has been my mind all along.”

sentences.zh: 」乃與巴東監軍柳純、南平太守夏侯承、宜都太守譚該等十餘人，俱露檄遠近，陳敦肆逆，率所統致討。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon, together with more than ten men including Liu Chun, Army Supervisor of Ba-East, Xiahou Cheng, grand administrator of Nanping, Tan Gai, grand administrator of Yidu, and others, he openly posted proclamations far and near, declaring Dun’s rebellion, and led the forces under his command to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Liu Chun, Xiahou Cheng, Tan Gai, and a dozen others in publishing a manifesto denouncing Wang Dun’s treason and marched every unit he commanded against him.

sentences.zh: 遣參軍司馬讚、孫雙奉表詣臺，參軍羅英至廣州，與陶侃剋期，參軍鄧騫、虞沖至長沙，令譙王承堅守。

translations.literal: He sent staff advisers Sima Zan and Sun Shuang to present a memorial at the capital, staff adviser Luo Ying to Guangzhou to fix a date with Tao Kan, staff advisers Deng Qian and Yu Chong to Changsha to order Prince Cheng of Qiao to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Sima Zan and Sun Shuang to court with a memorial, Luo Ying to Guangzhou to synchronize with Tao Kan, and Deng Qian and Yu Chong to Changsha to tell Prince Sima Cheng to stand fast.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍戴若思在江西，先得卓書，表上之，臺內皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the West, Dai Ruosi, was on the Jiangxi side; he first received Zhuo’s letter, presented it in a memorial, and everyone within the capital cried “Long live!”
translations.idiomatic: Dai Ruosi, west-conquering general on the Jiangxi front, got Zhuo’s letter first, forwarded it to court, and the whole capital erupted in cheers.

sentences.zh: 武昌大驚，傳卓軍至，人皆奔散。

translations.literal: Wuchang was greatly alarmed; rumor spread that Zhuo’s army had arrived, and people all fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Panic swept Wuchang when word spread that Gan Zhuo’s host was coming; the city emptied in terror.

sentences.zh: 詔書遷卓爲鎮南大將軍、侍中、都督荊梁二州諸軍事、荊州牧，梁州刺史如故，陶侃得卓信，即遣參軍高寶率兵下。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Zhuo to General Who Guards the South, Palace Attendant, commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Jing and Liang, and Governor of Jing Province, while his post as Inspector of Liang Province remained as before; when Tao Kan received Zhuo’s letter he at once sent his staff adviser Gao Bao to lead troops downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial orders raised Zhuo to General Who Guards the South, palace attendant, area commander for Jing and Liang, and shepherd of Jing while he kept Liang inspector; Tao Kan, reading Zhuo’s letter, immediately sent Gao Bao downriver with troops.

sentences.zh: 卓雖懷義正，而性不果毅，且年老多疑，計慮猶豫，軍次豬口，累旬不前。

translations.literal: Although Zhuo cherished righteous rectitude, by nature he was not resolute and firm, and moreover, being old, he was suspicious and hesitant in his plans; his army halted at Zhukou for many ten-day periods without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo meant well but lacked nerve; age had made him suspicious, and his army lingered at Zhukou for weeks without moving.

sentences.zh: 敦大懼，遣卓兄子行參軍卬求和，謝卓曰：「君此自是臣節，不相責也。

translations.literal: Dun was greatly frightened and sent Zhuo’s nephew, acting staff adviser Ang, to sue for peace, apologizing to Zhuo, saying, “What you are doing is itself the conduct of a minister—I do not blame you for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun panicked and sent Gan Ang, Zhuo’s nephew and acting adviser, to apologize: “Your stance is what a loyal minister would take—I do not reproach you.

sentences.zh: 吾家計急，不得不爾。

translations.literal: Our family’s situation is urgent; I could not do otherwise than this.
translations.idiomatic: My clan was cornered; I had no choice.

sentences.zh: 想便旋軍襄陽，當更結好。

translations.literal: I expect you will turn the army back to Xiangyang, and we shall renew our friendship.”
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will wheel back to Xiangyang so we can mend ties.”

sentences.zh: 」時王師敗績，敦求臺騶虞幡駐卓。

translations.literal: ” At that time the royal army had suffered defeat, and Dun requested a court groom with the Yu-plume banner to halt Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: By then the imperial army had lost; Wang Dun demanded a palace escort with the Yu banner to stop Gan Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓聞周顗、戴若思遇害，流涕謂卬曰：「吾之所憂，正謂今日。

translations.literal: When Zhuo heard that Zhou Yi and Dai Ruosi had been killed, he wept and said to Ang, “What I feared is precisely what has come today.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhou Yi and Dai Ruosi had been executed, Zhuo wept to Gan Ang, “This is exactly what I dreaded.

sentences.zh: 每得朝廷人書，常以胡寇爲先，不悟忽有蕭牆之禍。

translations.literal: Whenever I received letters from men of the court, they always put the Hu raiders first; I did not realize that suddenly there would be calamity within the inner walls.
translations.idiomatic: Court letters always warned of barbarians on the frontier; I never thought the blow would come from inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 且使聖上元吉，太子無恙，吾臨敦上流，亦未敢便危社稷。

translations.literal: Moreover, so long as the sage sovereign is supremely auspicious and the heir apparent is unharmed, though I press Dun from upstream, I still would not dare lightly to endanger the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: As long as the emperor and crown prince are safe, even pinning Wang Dun from upstream I would not lightly imperil the state.

sentences.zh: 吾適徑據武昌，敦勢逼，必劫天子以絕四海之望。

translations.literal: If I simply seize Wuchang directly, Dun’s position will be desperate and he is sure to seize the Son of Heaven to cut off the hopes of the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: If I seize Wuchang outright, Wang Dun will be cornered and will surely seize the emperor to break the world’s faith.

sentences.zh: 不如還襄陽，更思後圖。

translations.literal: It is better to return to Xiangyang and think again of a later plan.”
translations.idiomatic: Better to withdraw to Xiangyang and plan another move.”

sentences.zh: 」即命旋軍。

translations.literal: ” He immediately ordered the army to wheel about.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered an immediate retreat.

sentences.zh: 都尉秦康說卓曰：「今分兵取敦不難，但斷彭澤，上下不得相赴，自然離散，可一戰擒也。

translations.literal: Commandant Qin Kang said to Zhuo, “Now to divide forces and take Dun would not be difficult—only cut Pengze so that upper and lower cannot aid each other; they will naturally scatter apart, and he can be captured in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Kang urged him: “Split your force and cut Pengze; isolate Wang Dun’s upper and lower camps and you can shatter him in one stroke.

sentences.zh: 將軍既有忠節，中道而廢，更爲敗軍將，恐將軍之下亦各便求西還，不可得守也。

translations.literal: The general already holds loyal integrity; if you abandon it halfway and become again a defeated general, I fear that under your command each will seek to return west on his own, and you will not be able to hold them.”
translations.idiomatic: You have already pledged loyalty; to stop halfway makes you a beaten commander, and your men will scatter homeward—you cannot hold them.”

sentences.zh: 」卓不能從。

translations.literal: Zhuo could not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo would not listen.

sentences.zh: 樂道融亦日夜勸卓速下。

translations.literal: Yue Daorong likewise urged him day and night to hurry downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Daorong pressed him night and day to march downriver.

sentences.zh: 卓性先寬和，忽便強塞，徑還襄陽，意氣騷擾，舉動失常，自照鏡不見其頭，視庭樹而頭在樹上，心甚惡之。

translations.literal: Zhuo’s nature had always been mild and accommodating, but suddenly he became harsh and blocked; he went straight back to Xiangyang, his mood agitated, his actions abnormal; when he looked in a mirror he did not see his head, and when he gazed at the trees in the courtyard his head was in the tree—his heart was greatly sickened by this.
translations.idiomatic: Once easygoing, he turned obstinate, bolted for Xiangyang, grew feverish and erratic, saw his head vanish from the glass, then spotted it among the garden trees—a horror that preyed on him.

sentences.zh: 其家金櫃鳴，聲似槌鏡，清而悲。

translations.literal: In his house a metal coffer sounded, its noise like a mallet on a mirror, clear yet mournful.
translations.idiomatic: A bronze chest in his house rang like a hammer on bronze, bright and mournful.

sentences.zh: 巫云：「金櫃將離，是以悲鳴。

translations.literal: A shaman said, “The metal coffer is about to depart; therefore it wails.”
translations.idiomatic: A diviner said, “The coffer knows it will leave—hence the keening.”

sentences.zh: 」主簿何無忌及家人皆勸令自警。

translations.literal: ” Chief Clerk He Wuji and the whole household urged him to take warning.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk He Wuji and the family begged him to beware.

sentences.zh: 卓轉更很愎，聞諫輒怒。

translations.literal: Zhuo turned all the more cruel and obstinate; whenever he heard remonstrance he grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: He only grew more stubborn and raged at every warning.

sentences.zh: 方散兵使大佃，而不爲備。

translations.literal: He thereupon dispersed his troops for great reclamation farming and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: He stood his army down to giant reclamation projects and dropped all guard.

sentences.zh: 功曹榮建固諫，不納。

translations.literal: Merit assessor Rong Jian firmly remonstrated, but he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Jian, his merit clerk, pleaded in vain.

sentences.zh: 襄陽太守周慮等密承敦意，知卓無備，詐言湖中多魚，勸卓遣左右皆捕魚，乃襲害卓于寢，傳首于敦。

translations.literal: Grand administrators such as Zhou Lü of Xiangyang secretly obeyed Dun’s wishes; knowing Zhuo was unprepared, they falsely said there were many fish in the lake and urged Zhuo to send all his attendants to catch fish; then they attacked and killed Zhuo in his bedchamber and sent his head to Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lü of Xiangyang, secretly loyal to Wang Dun, knew Zhuo was undefended; he claimed the lake teemed with fish, sent Zhuo’s guards off fishing, then murdered Zhuo in his chamber and shipped the head to Wang Dun.

sentences.zh: 四子散騎郎蕃等皆被害。

translations.literal: His four sons, including Gentleman Cavalier Attendant Fan, were all put to death.
translations.idiomatic: His four sons, Fan and the rest, all died with him.

sentences.zh: 太寧中，追贈驃騎將軍，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: In the Taining years he was posthumously honored as General Who Inspires Might; his posthumous name was “Reverent.”
translations.idiomatic: During Taining he was posthumously named General Who Inspires Might with the style “Reverent.”

sentences.zh: 鄧騫字長真，長沙人。

translations.literal: Deng Qian, courtesy name Changzhen, was a native of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qian, style Changzhen, came from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 少有志氣，爲鄉鄰所重。

translations.literal: In youth he had high aspirations and was esteemed by his village neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: Even young he aimed high and won his neighbors’ respect.

sentences.zh: 常推誠行己，能以正直全於多難之時。

translations.literal: He always pushed sincerity in his conduct and was able, by uprightness, to preserve himself through many times of peril.
translations.idiomatic: He lived candidly and kept his integrity through repeated crises.

sentences.zh: 刺史譙王承命爲主簿，便說甘卓。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Qiao, the inspector, appointed him chief clerk, and he thereupon went to persuade Gan Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Prince Sima Cheng named him chief clerk and sent him to sway Gan Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 卓留爲參軍，欲與同行，以母老辭卓而反。

translations.literal: Zhuo kept him as a staff adviser and wished to travel with him, but Qian, citing his mother’s old age, declined Zhuo and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo kept him on staff and wanted him along the march; Qian pleaded an aged mother and went home instead.

sentences.zh: 承爲魏乂所敗，以虞悝兄弟爲承黨，乂盡誅之，而求騫甚急。

translations.literal: When Cheng was defeated by Wei Yi, because the Yu Kui brothers were treated as Cheng’s faction, Yi executed them all and urgently sought Qian.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Cheng lost to Wei Yi, the Yu Kui brothers died as Cheng’s partisans, and Wei Yi hunted Deng Qian fiercely.

sentences.zh: 鄉人皆爲之懼，騫笑曰：「欲用我耳。

translations.literal: His fellow villagers all feared for him; Qian smiled and said, “They only wish to employ me.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers trembled for him; he smiled, “They want my service.

sentences.zh: 彼新得州，多殺忠良，是其求賢之時，豈以行人爲罪！

translations.literal: They have newly taken the province and have killed many loyal and good men; this is the time when they seek worthies—how could they treat an envoy as a criminal!”
translations.idiomatic: They just seized the province and have slaughtered loyal men—this is when they crave talent; they will not punish a messenger!”

sentences.zh: 」乃往詣乂。

translations.literal: ” He therefore went to visit Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He walked straight into Wei Yi’s camp.

sentences.zh: 乂喜曰：「君所謂古之解揚也。

translations.literal: Yi was pleased and said, “You are what they call an ancient Jie Yang.”
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yi beamed: “You are a Jie Yang for our age.”

sentences.zh: 」以爲別駕。

translations.literal: ” He appointed him aide-de-camp.
translations.idiomatic: He named him aide-de-camp.

sentences.zh: 騫有節操忠信，兼識量弘遠，善與人交，久而益敬。

translations.literal: Qian had integrity, faithfulness, and breadth of judgment and foresight; he was skilled in dealing with people, and the longer one knew him the more one revered him.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qian was loyal, steady, and far-sighted; his friendships deepened into reverence over time.

sentences.zh: 太尉庾亮稱之，以爲長者。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yu Liang praised him and deemed him a man of mature virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Grand commandant Yu Liang hailed him as an elder statesman in spirit.
