translations.literal: When Wen Qiao and others arrived, Jun was suspicious of court gentlemen, and because Chao was especially favored by the emperor, he suspected Chao above all.
translations.idiomatic: After Wen Qiao came, Su Jun doubly distrusted Liu Chao for his closeness to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 後王導出奔，超與懷德令匡術、建康令管旆等密謀，將欲奉帝而出。

translations.literal: Later Wang Dao fled; Chao together with Magistrate of Huaide Kuang Shu, Magistrate of Jiankang Guan Pei, and others secretly plotted intending to escort the emperor out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao fled; Liu Chao, Kuang Shu of Huaide, Guan Pei of Jiankang, and others plotted to smuggle the emperor out.

sentences.zh: 未及期，事泄，峻使任讓將兵入收超及鍾雅。

translations.literal: Before the date arrived, the affair leaked; Jun sent Ren Rang with troops to enter and seize Chao and Zhong Ya.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked; Ren Rang’s troops seized Liu Chao and Zhong Ya.

sentences.zh: [5]帝抱持悲泣曰：「還我侍中、右衛！

translations.literal: [5] The emperor embraced them, weeping in grief, and said, “Give me back my palace attendant and right guard!”
translations.idiomatic: [5] The boy emperor clung to them, sobbing, “Give me back my attendants!”

sentences.zh: 」任讓不奉詔，因害之。

translations.literal: ” Ren Rang did not obey the edict and therefore killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Rang ignored the plea and murdered them.

sentences.zh: 及峻平，任讓與陶侃有舊，侃欲特不誅之，乃請於帝。

translations.literal: When Jun was crushed, Ren Rang had old ties with Tao Kan; Kan wished specially not to execute him and therefore petitioned the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun fell, Tao Kan—old friend of Ren Rang—begged to spare him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「讓是殺我侍中、右衛者，不可宥。

translations.literal: The emperor said, “Rang is the one who killed my palace attendant and right guard; he cannot be forgiven.”
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng answered: “Ren Rang killed my ministers—he cannot live.”

sentences.zh: 」由是遂誅讓。

translations.literal: ” On this account Rang was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Rang died on the order.

sentences.zh: 及超將改葬，帝痛念之不已，詔遷高顯近地葬之，使出入得瞻望其墓。

translations.literal: When Chao was about to be reburied, the emperor grieved and thought of him without end; he issued an edict to move the grave to high, illustrious, nearby ground so that going in and out he could gaze on the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Reburying Liu Chao, the emperor moved the tomb to a lofty nearby hill so he could see it coming and going.

sentences.zh: 追贈衛尉，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Minister of the Guards, posthumous name “Loyal.”
translations.idiomatic: The court named him minister of the guards posthumously, styled “Loyal.”

sentences.zh: 超天性謙慎，歷事三帝，恒在機密，並蒙親遇，而不敢因寵驕諂，故士人皆安而敬之。

translations.literal: Chao by nature was humble and careful; he served three emperors in succession, always in secretarial closeness, and all favored him with intimacy, yet he did not dare, because of favor, to become arrogant or flattering; therefore gentlemen were at ease with him and revered him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chao served three emperors in the inner chancery, won constant favor, yet never turned proud or sycophantic—so peers trusted and honored him.

sentences.zh: 子訥嗣，謹飭有石慶之風，歷中書侍郎、下邳內史。

translations.literal: His son Ne succeeded; he was cautious and restrained in the manner of Shi Qing’s household, and rose through gentleman of the secretariat to interior minister of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: His heir Liu Ne was as scrupulous as Shi Qing’s sons, rising to secretariat gentleman and Xiapi interior minister.

sentences.zh: 訥子享，亦清慎，爲散騎郎。

translations.literal: Ne’s son Xiang was likewise clear and careful and was Gentleman Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Ne’s son Liu Xiang stayed sober and spare as gentleman cavalier.

sentences.zh: 鍾雅字彥冑，潁川長社人也。

translations.literal: Zhong Ya, courtesy name Yanzhou, was a native of Changshe in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ya, style Yanzhou, came from Changshe in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 父曅，公府掾，早終。

translations.literal: His father Ye was a clerk in the princely administration and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhong Ye served the princely administration and died young.

sentences.zh: 雅少孤，好學有才志，舉四行，除汝陽令，入爲佐著作郎。

translations.literal: Ya in youth was orphaned, loved learning and had talent and aspiration; he was raised on the four conduct categories, was appointed magistrate of Ruyang, and entered as assistant gentleman editor.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he loved books, passed the four-conduct recommendation, governed Ruyang, then joined the editorial office.

sentences.zh: 母憂去官，服闋復職。

translations.literal: He left office for mourning for his mother; when mourning was completed he resumed duty.
translations.idiomatic: Mother’s death took him home; when mourning ended he returned.

sentences.zh: 東海王越請爲參軍，遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: Prince Sima Yue of the East Sea asked him to be a staff adviser, and he was promoted to gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue made him adviser, then palace gentleman.

sentences.zh: 避亂東渡，元帝以爲丞相記室參軍，遷臨淮內史、振威將軍。

translations.literal: Fleeing turmoil he crossed east; Emperor Yuan made him recorder-clerk on the chancellor’s staff, promoted him to interior minister of Linhuai, and General Who Rouses Might.
translations.idiomatic: He fled east and became Yuan’s chancellor recorder, then Linhuai interior minister and General Who Rouses Might.

sentences.zh: 頃之，徵拜散騎侍郎，轉尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Gentleman Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and transferred to right aide of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, then right secretariat aide.

sentences.zh: 時有事於太廟，雅奏曰：「陛下繼承世數，於京兆府君爲玄孫，而今祝文稱曾孫，恐此因循之失，宜見改正。

translations.literal: At that time there was a ceremony in the Grand Temple; Ya memorialized, saying, “Your Majesty continues the generational count and toward the Lord of Jingzhao is great-great-grandson, yet now the prayer text calls you ‘great-grandson’; I fear this is a slip of routine and ought to be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: During a grand temple rite he noted the prayer called the emperor “great-grandson” to the spirit of Sima Fang when the true degree was great-great-grandson—he asked a fix.

sentences.zh: 又禮，祖之昆弟，從祖父也。

translations.literal: Moreover, by ritual the elder brother of a grandfather is a “grand uncle.”
translations.idiomatic: Ritual also names a grandfather’s elder brother correctly.

sentences.zh: 景皇帝自以功德爲世宗，不以伯祖而登廟，亦宜除伯祖之文。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing on his own, by merit and virtue, became Shizong of the line and did not ascend the temple as grand-uncle; the wording of grand-uncle should likewise be removed.”
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing became lineage Shizong on merit, not as grand-uncle—so that phrase should go.”

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「禮，事宗廟，自曾孫已下皆稱曾孫，此非因循之失也。

translations.literal: ” An edict said, “By ritual, in serving the ancestral temple, from great-grandson downward all are called ‘great-grandson’; this is not a slip of routine.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered: “Ritual calls every generation below ‘great-grandson’ at the altar—that is not a copyist’s error.

sentences.zh: 義取於重孫，可歷世共其名，無所改也。

translations.literal: The meaning is taken from ‘weighty descendant’; they may share the title through generations; nothing is to be changed.
translations.idiomatic: The term stacks generations; leave it.

sentences.zh: 稱伯祖不安，如所奏。

translations.literal: Calling ‘grand-uncle’ is improper, as you memorialized.”
translations.idiomatic: The ‘grand-uncle’ line is wrong—remove it as you say.”

sentences.zh: 」轉北軍中候。

translations.literal: ” He was transferred to colonel of the northern armies.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to colonel of the northern armies.

sentences.zh: 大將軍王敦請爲從事中郎，補宣城內史。

translations.literal: Grand General Wang Dun asked him to be attendant clerk and filled the vacancy as interior minister of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun named him staff aide and Xuancheng interior minister.

sentences.zh: 錢鳳作逆，加廣武將軍，率眾屯青弋。

translations.literal: When Qian Feng rebelled, he was additionally named General Who Displays Martiality and led a host to garrison at Qingyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Feng rose he added the title General Who Displays Martiality and camped at Qingyi.

sentences.zh: 時廣德縣人周玘爲鳳起兵攻雅，雅退據涇縣，收合士庶，討玘，斬之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou Qi of Guangde county raised troops for Feng to attack Ya; Ya withdrew to defend Jing county, gathered gentry and commoners, campaigned against Qi, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: A local Zhou Qi struck for Qian Feng; Zhong Ya fell back to Jing, rallied townsmen, killed Zhou Qi.

sentences.zh: 鳳平，徵拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Feng was crushed, he was summoned as left aide of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Qian Feng fell he became left secretariat aide.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, he was promoted to imperial censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming’s death raised him to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 時國喪未期，而尚書梅陶私奏女妓，雅劾奏曰：「臣聞放勛之殂，八音遏密，雖在凡庶，猶能三載。

translations.literal: At that time the state mourning had not yet reached one year, yet Palace Secretary Mei Tao privately presented female musicians; Ya impeached him, saying, “I have heard that when Yao (Fangxun) passed, the eight sounds were stopped and sealed; even among common folk they still observe three years.
translations.idiomatic: While Ming’s mourning was unfinished, Mei Tao sent singing girls; Zhong Ya impeached: “When Yao died even commoners silenced music for three years.”

sentences.zh: 自茲以來，歷代所同。

translations.literal: From this onward, the dynasties have been the same.
translations.idiomatic: Every dynasty has done the same.

sentences.zh: 肅祖明皇帝崩背萬國，當期來月。

translations.literal: Revered ancestor Emperor Ming has passed from the myriad regions; the full year will arrive next month.
translations.idiomatic: Our late Emperor Ming has left the world; his first anniversary nears.

sentences.zh: 聖主縞素，泣血臨朝，百僚慘愴，動無歡容。

translations.literal: The sage ruler in hemp and white, weeping blood, faces court; the hundred officials are dismal and mournful, and in movement there is no cheerful countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The court wears hemp and tears; no face shows joy.

sentences.zh: 陶無大臣忠慕之節，家庭侈靡，聲妓紛葩，絲竹之音，流聞衢路，宜加放黜，以整王憲。

translations.literal: Mei Tao lacks the integrity of a great minister’s loyal longing; his household is extravagant, singing girls throng, and the sound of strings and bamboo flows out to the lanes—he ought to be banished to set straight the royal statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Tao shows no minister’s grief—his house rings with music; banish him to mend the statute.

sentences.zh: 請下司徒，論正清議。

translations.literal: I ask that it be sent down to the Situ for discussion and rectification under pure discussion.”
translations.idiomatic: Send the case to the Situ for “pure discussion” censure.”

sentences.zh: 」穆后臨朝，特原不問。

translations.literal: ” When Empress Dowager Mu held court, she specially pardoned him and did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Mu pardoned Mei Tao.

sentences.zh: 雅直法繩違，百僚皆憚之。

translations.literal: Ya applied the law straight to strike violations, and the hundred officials all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ya enforced the code; every minister feared him.

sentences.zh: 北中郎將劉遐卒，遐部曲作亂，詔郭默討之，以雅監征討軍事、假節。

translations.literal: General of the Center, Liu Xia, died; Xia’s personal troops made rebellion; an edict ordered Guo Mo to campaign against them, with Ya supervising the punitive expedition and holding credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xia’s bodyguard mutinied, Guo Mo marched under Zhong Ya’s staff command.

sentences.zh: 事平，拜驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was appointed General Who Dashes the Enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Peace made him General Who Dashes the Enemy.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之難，詔雅爲前鋒監軍、假節，領精勇千人以距峻。

translations.literal: During the crisis of Su Jun, an edict made Ya vanguard supervisor, with credential staff, leading a thousand picked brave men to resist Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun’s revolt made him vanguard supervisor with a thousand picked men.

sentences.zh: 雅以兵少，不敢擊，退還。

translations.literal: Ya, because the troops were few, did not dare strike and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He dared not attack with so few and fell back.

sentences.zh: 拜侍中。

translations.literal: He was appointed palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was named palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋王師敗績，雅與劉超並侍衛天子。

translations.literal: Soon the royal army was routed, and Ya together with Liu Chao both attended and guarded the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When the army broke, he and Liu Chao stayed with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 或謂雅曰：「見可而進，知難而退，古之道也。

translations.literal: Someone said to Ya, “When you see the fit, advance; when you know the difficulty, retire—the way of antiquity is so.
translations.idiomatic: A friend urged him: “Advance when you can, retreat when you must—that was the ancients’ way.

sentences.zh: 君性亮直，必不容於寇讎，何不隨時之宜而坐待其斃。

translations.literal: Your nature is bright and straight; you are sure not to be tolerated by the bandit foe—why not follow the timely expedient and sit waiting for their doom?”
translations.idiomatic: You are too straight for rebels—why not slip away and wait them out?”

sentences.zh: 」雅曰：「國亂不能匡，君危不能濟，各遜遁以求免，吾懼董狐執簡而至矣。

translations.literal: ” Ya said, “When the state is in turmoil and I cannot set it aright, when the lord is in peril and I cannot save him, if each slinks away to seek escape, I fear that Dong Hu will arrive with his bamboo slip in hand.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ya answered: “If I flee while the throne totters, Dong Hu will write my shame in his chronicle.”

sentences.zh: 」庾亮臨去，顧謂雅曰：「後事深以相委。

translations.literal: ” When Yu Liang was about to depart, he turned and said to Ya, “The later affair I deeply entrust to you.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang, leaving, turned: “I leave what follows to you.”

sentences.zh: 」雅曰：「棟折榱崩，誰之責也？

translations.literal: ” Ya said, “When the ridgepole breaks and the rafters collapse, whose fault is it?”
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ya shot back: “When the roof falls, whose fault is that?”

sentences.zh: 」亮曰：「今日之事，不容復言，卿當期剋復之效耳。

translations.literal: ” Liang said, “Today’s affair brooks no more words; you must expect the effect of recovery.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang said: “No more blame talk—you must win restoration.”

sentences.zh: 」雅曰：「想足下不愧荀林父耳。

translations.literal: ” Ya said, “I suppose you will not shame Xun Linfu.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ya: “See that you do not disgrace Xun Linfu.”

sentences.zh: 」及峻逼遷車駕幸石頭，雅、超流涕步從。

translations.literal: ” When Jun forced the removal of the imperial carriage to Stone Citadel, Ya and Chao wept and followed on foot.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun marched the court to Stone Citadel, the two walked behind weeping.

sentences.zh: 明年，並爲賊所害。

translations.literal: In the following year both were killed by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the rebels killed them both.

sentences.zh: 賊平，追贈光祿勳。

translations.literal: When the rebels were crushed, he was posthumously awarded Minister of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory he was posthumously named minister of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 其後以家貧，詔賜布帛百匹。

translations.literal: Later, because his household was poor, an edict granted one hundred bolts of cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Later edicts sent a hundred bolts of silk for his poverty.

sentences.zh: 子誕，位至中軍參軍，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Dan rose to staff adviser of the central army and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong Dan became central army adviser and died young.

sentences.zh: 【史評】

translations.literal: 【Historians’ appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Section title: Historians’ appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：應詹行業聿修，文史足用，入居列位，則嘉謀屢陳；

translations.literal: The historians say: In conduct and vocation Ying Zhan was constantly cultivated, sufficient in letters and histories; when he entered to occupy successive posts, fine plans were repeatedly offered;
translations.idiomatic: The annalists write: Ying Zhan refined conduct and letters; in central office his counsel flowed;

sentences.zh: 出撫藩條，則惠政斯洽。

translations.literal: when he went out to soothe the regional cords, benevolent government spread everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: in the provinces his rule ran kind and clear.

sentences.zh: 甘卓伐暴寧亂，庸績克宣，作鎮扞城，威略具舉。

translations.literal: Gan Zhuo smote cruelty and pacified turmoil, common achievement was duly proclaimed; established as a bulwark he defended the walls, might and strategy both displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo crushed rebels and held the frontier with equal parts force and guile.

sentences.zh: 及兇渠犯順，志在勤王。

translations.literal: When the wicked chieftain offended the right, his intent was fixed on aiding the king.
translations.idiomatic: When traitors faced the throne he meant to save it.

sentences.zh: 既而人撓其謀，天奪其鑒，疑留不斷，自取誅夷。

translations.literal: Yet men thwarted his plans, Heaven took away his mirror; hesitating and lingering undecided, he brought execution on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Men blocked him, Heaven dimmed his sight; his wavering bought his death.

sentences.zh: 卞壼束帶立朝，以匡正爲己任；

translations.literal: Bian Kun, girded and standing in court, took correction as his own charge;
translations.idiomatic: Bian Kun belted his robe and meant to straighten the court;

sentences.zh: 褰裳衛主，蹈忠義以成名。

translations.literal: lifting his robe he guarded the sovereign, treading loyalty and righteousness to make a name.
translations.idiomatic: he hitched his robe and died for loyalty’s name.

sentences.zh: 遂使臣死於君，子死於父，惟忠與孝，萃其一門。

translations.literal: Thus the minister died for the lord, the sons died for the father—only loyalty and filial piety were gathered in one gate.
translations.idiomatic: Father and sons died for sovereign and parent alike—loyalty and filial piety in one gate.

sentences.zh: 古稱社稷之臣，忠貞之謂矣。

translations.literal: What antiquity called a minister of the altars of soil and grain is just this sense of loyal truth.
translations.idiomatic: They are what antiquity meant by “pillars of the state.”

sentences.zh: 劉超勤肅奉上，鍾雅正直當官。

translations.literal: Liu Chao was diligent and austere in serving his superiors; Zhong Ya was upright in holding office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chao served with tireless care; Zhong Ya held office straight.

sentences.zh: 屬巨猾滔天，幼君危逼，乃崎嶇寇難，契闊艱虞，匪石爲心，寒松比操，貞軌皆沒，亮跡雙升。

translations.literal: They met a monstrous villain flooding heaven, the young sovereign pressed to the brink; then they twisted through bandit hardship, endured every trial—hearts not stone, conduct likened to winter pine; both kept the chaste track and together rose in bright traces.
translations.idiomatic: Under a usurper’s flood they clung to a boy emperor, hearts like ice-pines, and rose in martyrdom together.

sentences.zh: 雖高赫在難彌恭，荀息繼之以死，方之二子，曾何足云！

translations.literal: Although Gao He in peril grew ever more reverent, and Xun Xi followed with his death, compared with these two men, how can those suffice even to speak of them!
translations.idiomatic: Gao He’s reverence in danger and Xun Xi’s suicide scarcely match these two.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：卓臨南服，詹蒞西州。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Zhuo faced the southern domain, Zhan governed the western province.
translations.idiomatic: The hymn says: Zhuo held the south, Ying Zhan the west.

sentences.zh: [6]政刑克舉，威惠兼修。

translations.literal: [6] Punishments and government were duly raised, awe and kindness both cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: [6] Law ran clear, kindness and terror paired.

sentences.zh: 應嗟運促，甘斃疑留。

translations.literal: Ying lamented a fate cut short; Gan perished through doubt’s delay.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhan’s life ran short; Gan Zhuo died of hesitation.

sentences.zh: 望之徇義，處死爲易。

translations.literal: Wangzhi followed righteousness; facing death came easily.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Kun chose righteousness; death came as ease.

sentences.zh: 惟子惟臣，名節斯寄。

translations.literal: As son, as minister, to those names and nodes he entrusted himself.
translations.idiomatic: Son and minister hung all on name and duty.

sentences.zh: 鍾劉入仕，忠貞攸履。

translations.literal: Zhong and Liu entered service, treading loyalty and truth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Ya and Liu Chao walked the path of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 竭其股肱，繼之以死。

translations.literal: They exhausted their arms and thighs, and death followed upon that.
translations.idiomatic: They gave sinew and bone to the throne, then gave life.
